Reading an .env file without an explicit encoding should default to UTF-8, while callers that explicitly pass another encoding must keep that behavior. Public report: https://github.com/theskumar/python-dotenv/issues/207

report.root_cause: When no explicit encoding is provided, the function falls back to the system locale encoding (via locale.getpreferredencoding). On systems where the locale is ASCII, reading a UTF‑8 .env file raises UnicodeDecodeError.
report.summary: Set the library's default encoding to UTF‑8 so read_env defaults to UTF‑8 instead of the locale when no encoding argument is given.
report.evidence: The test patches locale.getpreferredencoding to return "ascii" and expects read_env to correctly read a UTF‑8 .env file. The current implementation selects the locale encoding, causing a UnicodeDecodeError. Changing DEFAULT_ENCODING to "utf-8" ensures read_env uses UTF‑8 by default, satisfying the test.
